ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There is a large circle in the figure, with a square of side length 1 embedded in the upper right. The lower-left corner of the square appears to be the center of the large circle, and the upper-left corner and lower-right corner of the square are respectively on the large circle, so the radius of the large circle is 1. The small circle is located at the upper-right corner of the square, tangent respectively to the top side and right side of the square, and tangent to the large circle. Reasoning: Let the lower-left corner of the square, that is, the center of the large circle, be (0,0), and the square region be 0≤x≤1, 0≤y≤1, then the equation of the large circle is x^2+y^2=1. Let the radius of the small circle be r. Since the small circle is tangent to the top side y=1 and the right side x=1 of the square, its center is (1-r, 1-r). The small circle is externally tangent to the large circle, so the distance between the two circle centers equals 1+r. Therefore: sqrt((1-r)^2+(1-r)^2)=1+r, that is sqrt(2)(1-r)=1+r. Solving gives sqrt(2)-sqrt(2)r=1+r, so sqrt(2)-1=(sqrt(2)+1)r, r=(sqrt(2)-1)/(sqrt(2)+1)=(sqrt(2)-1)^2.

raw_record.question_text: In the diagram, the square has side length 1. What is the radius of the small circle?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: a unit square sits in the upper-right quadrant of a large circle. The lower-left corner of the square is the center of the large circle, and the square’s top-left and bottom-right corners lie on the large circle, so the large circle has radius 1. The small circle is tucked into the top-right corner of the square, tangent to the square’s top and right sides and tangent externally to the large circle. Set coordinates with the lower-left corner of the square/center of the large circle at (0,0), the square occupying 0≤x≤1, 0≤y≤1, and the large circle x^2+y^2=1. If the small circle radius is r, its center is (1-r,1-r). Because it is externally tangent to the large circle of radius 1, the distance from (0,0) to (1-r,1-r) is 1+r. Thus sqrt((1-r)^2+(1-r)^2)=1+r, so sqrt(2)(1-r)=1+r. Solving gives r=(sqrt(2)-1)/(sqrt(2)+1)=(sqrt(2)-1)^2.

推理：设正方形左下角，也就是大圆圆心为 (0,0)，正方形区域为 0≤x≤1, 0≤y≤1，则大圆方程为 x^2+y^2=1。设小圆半径为 r。由于小圆与正方形上边 y=1 和右边 x=1 相切，它的圆心是 (1-r, 1-r)。小圆与大圆外切，所以两个圆心距离等于 1+r。因此：sqrt((1-r)^2+(1-r)^2)=1+r，即 sqrt(2)(1-r)=1+r。解得 sqrt(2)-sqrt(2)r=1+r，所以 sqrt(2)-1=(sqrt(2)+1)r，r=(sqrt(2)-1)/(sqrt(2)+1)=(sqrt(2)-1)^2。
